slot.brief: System of three equations with a parameter; find the value for which it has infinitely many solutions by checking Δ = 0 and consistency.

stem: The system $x+y+z=1$, $x+2y+2z=4$, $x+\lambda y+4z=10$ has infinitely many solutions when $\lambda$ is:

verdicts.working: Subtract the first equation from the second and third to get y + z = 3 and (lambda - 1)y + 3z = 9. For infinitely many solutions, the latter must be three times the former, so lambda - 1 = 3 and lambda = 4.

working:
$\Delta=\begin{vmatrix}1&1&1\\1&2&2\\1&\lambda&4\end{vmatrix}=4-\lambda$, so $\Delta=0$ gives $\lambda=4$. Then Eq. (3) $=3\,\text{Eq. (2)}-2\,\text{Eq. (1)}$, including the right-hand sides: $10=3(4)-2(1)$. The first two coefficient rows are independent, so the consistent system has infinitely many solutions.

Independent check: Subtract the first equation from the second and third to get y + z = 3 and (lambda - 1)y + 3z = 9. For infinitely many solutions, the latter must be three times the former, so lambda - 1 = 3 and lambda = 4.
solution: For infinitely many solutions, the third equation must be dependent on the first two. At $\lambda=4$, its left-hand side is $3$ times equation (2) minus $2$ times equation (1), and $3(4)-2(1)=10$ on the right-hand side as well. Thus the system is consistent with dependent equations, giving infinitely many solutions.
